genericProblem: A UI import or refresh rule can promote app-substrate transport into a screen primitive, or describe a cache-generation invariant too broadly, causing a later page implementation to violate the single-API boundary or retain a stale local view after a valid context change.

counterexamples.reason: scopeRef/projectId is an operation-specific business argument here, so it must not be removed or generalized into a claim that every list cache key has only contextVersion.
platformHttpProtocol is a foundation transport dependency, not evidence that a page may build protocol headers.
The current query context includes identityKey, but there is no generated operation consumer; this is dormant generic context, not authority to invent a consumer.

findings.finding: The physical screen denominator incorrectly lists createObservedBaseQuery and platformHttpProtocol as screen-level imports although createObservedBaseQuery is consumed only by the two app API substrates and platformHttpProtocol has no app-side consumer.

A contextVersion change recomputes generated query arguments but does not remount the operations content component; pagination and other local visual state can therefore survive a context switch and request an empty later page.

contextVersion is the mandatory cache-generation input for every owner-scoped read, but scopeRef/projectId remains a separate required business argument for the concrete operations that declare it; identityKey has no current generated read consumer.

The design did not make the generated-hook/generated-client read-write boundary, tag invalidation, and context-generation refresh distinguishable, leaving a path for page-local fetch, refetch loop, or refresh-key duplication.
The selected platform workspace state owner was underspecified despite the existing app-owned React state implementation; an implementer could incorrectly add Redux state.

preventionDispositions.reason: Maintain separate exact denominators for screen primitives and app-substrate primitives; a screen import-equality rule may not require transport construction or protocol-header construction.
Every context-switching host must specify the shared local-view reset boundary and a focused red mutation.
The roster states the finite distinction between mandatory context generation, operation-specific scopeRef and dormant identityKey.
The common UI contract distinguishes generated reads, generated-client writes, tag invalidation, and context-generation refresh while forbidding page-local fetch/refetch/refresh-key loops.
The platform workspace selector is explicitly bound to existing app-owned React state and prohibited from adding a slice or reducer.
